tagline: The Visayas hub — a dense island cluster where every high-value trip already crosses water.
summary: Cebu is the central Philippines' commercial and tourism hub, anchored by Cebu City and Mactan Island (home to the international airport and the Mactan resort strip). The surrounding Central Visayas is a tight archipelago — Bohol/Panglao, Camotes, Mactan, Dumaguete, Siquijor — where ferries and bangka boats are the connective tissue. Resort transfers, island-hopping day trips, and inter-island commuting are constant and currently served by conventional fast ferries (OceanJet and peers) and small craft. The flows are enormous and proven: Mactan-Cebu airport handled 11.3 million passengers in 2024 and neighbouring Bohol drew roughly 1.37 million visitors, all of whom cross water to reach the islands. Pioneer II covers the dense inner-Visayas hops; Quanta LR opens longer inter-island and Manila-facing line-hauls.

use_cases.title: Airport & resort premium transfers
use_cases.body: Direct water transfers from Mactan-Cebu airport to the Mactan resort strip and across to Bohol/Panglao, bypassing congested bridges and giving arriving guests a premium first leg.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Cebu is a textbook dense-archipelago hub: Pioneer II's 70 nm all-electric envelope covers the high-frequency core — Cebu ↔ Bohol/Panglao (~40 nm), Mactan airport transfers (~8 nm) and Cebu ↔ Camotes (~28 nm) — over short, sheltered inner-Visayas water with shore charging at established piers.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta LR's ~2,000 nm hybrid range, with no charging-infrastructure dependency, handles the longer Negros (Dumaguete ~90 nm), Leyte and Manila-facing line-hauls that fall outside the electric envelope.

competitive_landscape: OceanJet and other fast-ferry operators run the established inter-island network — demand proof and potential partners, not threats.
seasonality: Year-round; habagat (SW monsoon, ~Jun–Oct) and typhoon season elevates cancellation risk on small craft — the reliability hook for a more capable platform. Amihan (NE, Dec–Feb) is peak.
regulatory_note: Coordinate with MARINA (Maritime Industry Authority), Philippine Ports Authority, and Cebu/LGU port operators. Cabotage and domestic-flag rules apply.
precedents: Indonesian and Maldivian island-hopping clusters in the atlas show resort + airport transfer as the entry pattern for hospitality-led marine mobility.
